title: The old sage weeps
hook: the sage Asita holds the baby, smiles, then weeps: he will not live to hear this child teach

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lumbini, a birth in a garden on the road between two homes. Born on the way somewhere.

Gods in the sky, the story says, celebrating: waving their cloaks, shouting for joy. An old seer named Asita, resting in his daytime retreat, sees them and asks why. They tell him: in the land of the Sakyas, a child has been born who will one day turn the wheel of the teaching. So the old man hurries to King Suddhodana's palace and asks to see the baby. The king brings the child out, and Asita takes him in his arms.
screen: `THE GODS ARE CELEBRATING.` → `AN OLD SEER HURRIES TO THE PALACE.` → `HE HOLDS THE BABY.`

segments.voice: This story is told in verse, in a collection called the Sutta Nipata. Asita holds the baby and looks at him closely, the way an expert looks at something rare. He reads the marks on the child's body, and he's sure. Joyful, he lifts his voice: this one is supreme, the highest among people. Then, holding the child, the old man starts to cry. The Sakyans are frightened. Is something wrong with the baby? Is danger coming? No, Asita tells them. Nothing bad will happen to this child. He'll reach the highest awakening, teach out of compassion for many, and his way of life will spread far. I'm weeping for myself. My life is nearly over. I'll be gone before he teaches, and I won't be there to hear it. It's a strange, tender moment this early in the story: the one who sees clearly who this child is knows he'll never see it come true. But Asita doesn't only grieve. He goes to his nephew, a young man named Nalaka, and tells him: when you hear that someone has awakened and is teaching, go to him. Follow him. Years later, the story says, Nalaka does. The old man couldn't reach the future himself, so he sent someone into it: a seed planted in a garden he knew he'd never walk in.
screen: `ASITA READS THE MARKS.` · `THE HIGHEST AMONG PEOPLE.` · `I WON'T LIVE TO HEAR HIM.` · `HE SENDS HIS NEPHEW, NALAKA.` · then, large: `PLANT IT ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a good thing you won't see finished: a tree you planted, a child or student you won't see grown, a cause longer than your life, a kindness rippling somewhere you'll never know. Hold it the way Asita held the child, close and with open hands. If sadness and joy both come, let both be there.
Asita. The old seer who held the newborn, knew who he'd become, wept because he wouldn't live to hear him teach, and sent his nephew instead.
Your line: plant it anyway, even in a garden you won't walk in. That's day twenty-four.

howItsDone: Buddhists tell the story of Asita as part of the Buddha's birth, and in Theravada communities the Nalaka Sutta is recited and studied; the scene of Asita holding the infant appears in temple art across Asia.

original.note: Pali and Sanskrit: a name meaning dark or black (a- + sita, white).

trapdoor: what you thought: an old man cries at a baby.
what it means: the sage who recognizes the child weeps because he won't live to hear him, and sends his nephew into a future he can't reach.
what a scholar hears: the Nalaka Sutta (Sutta Nipata 3.11) tells the story in verse; later tradition calls the sage Kaladevala.

chat.says: Why would an old sage cry while holding a baby he called special?
options: He was sad he'd die before the child grew up and taught.
He saw danger ahead for the child and was afraid for him.
He was let down that the child would be a king, not a sage.
chat.meaning: Asita said nothing bad would happen to the child. He wept for himself: he'd be gone before the child taught.

Asita.meaning: the old seer who held the newborn and wept

Sakyas.meaning: the Buddha's own people, his clan

Sutta Nipata.meaning: an early collection of Buddhist teachings in verse

Nalaka.meaning: Asita's nephew, told to follow the child when he taught

notes: Sn 3.11 paraphrased (Fausbøll's 1881 translation is public domain but not on the validator's list, so nothing is quoted). Asita's words are given as paraphrase, not quotation. Confirm.
The detail that Asita 'reads the marks' is in the verses (he examines the child); confirm wording.
The etymology of Asita (dark, a- + sita) in the original note: confirm.
Alternative name Kaladevala is from the commentaries (Nidanakatha). Confirm.
